sources.citation: Bergman, Richard and Gray, Ian and Gray, Claire (1969). The Phonology of Tampulma. Institute of African Studies.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number 2235.17.50 no.9)
sources.note: The catalog has no record and no existing statement for Tampulma; this work adds a two-tone system (H/L, syllable TBU) but is silent on stress, so nothing to agree or disagree with. Note the open_url points at the Rosetta 'vertxt-1' part (Section 12, a glossed folk-tale text with tone marks, no analysis); the phonology proper is the sibling item rosettaproject_tpm_phon-1, which I read in full.

sources.citation: Bergman, Richard, Ian Gray & Claire Gray. 1969. Collected field reports on the phonology of Tampulma (Collected Language Notes 9). Legon/Accra: Institute of African Studies, University of Ghana. viii+53 pp. [Rosetta Project scans on archive.org: items rosettaproject_tpm_phon-1 (Sections 2-10, pp.1-38), contents-1, detail-1 (Sec.1 Introduction), ortho-1 (Sec.11), vertxt-1 (Sec.12 Text)]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number 2235.17.50 no.9)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.3 'The Word' (pp.1-2) marks word boundaries by vowel harmony and glottal stop only; Sec. 9 'Supra-Segmental Features' (pp.26-28) contains only 9.1 Length and 9.2 Tone: 'In Tampulma the syllable is the tone bearing unit. There are two phonemic tones, high and low', plus downdrift, downstep and tone perturbation rules. The words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur anywhere in the scanned sections (scanned a full-text search for stress/accent + page images pp.1-2, 26-28 checked).

sources.citation: Brindle, Jonathan. 2017. A dictionary and grammatical outline of Chakali (African Language Grammars and Dictionaries 2). Berlin: Language Science Press. [sister Southern-Grusi language; tone section]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Second-hand on Tampulma tone only: 'Vagla, Dɛg, Tampulma, Sisaala, and Pasaale are all described with two tones (Rowland & Rowland 1965; Crouch & Smiles 1966; Bergman, Gray & Gray 1969..)'. Nothing on Tampulma stress.
